title: Life-science agents cut the artifact-vs-text gap below 10 points by H2 2027
body: LifeSciBench's most durable finding is not the ~36.1% headline pass rate but the artifact gap: OpenAI's GPT-Rosalind scored 45.1% on text-only tasks yet collapsed to 28.1% the moment a task required parsing a real scientific artifact — a genomic sequence file, a chemical-structure file, raw experimental data, or a URL pointing to one. That 17-point cliff isolates the bottleneck for autonomous science: models can reason fluently about biology in prose but stumble on the data objects a working scientist actually manipulates. This prediction holds that the next round of life-science research-agent work will treat the artifact gap as the explicit optimization target, because it is the cleanest, most cited weakness a vendor or lab can move. The concrete, falsifiable claim is that by the second half of 2027 a named life-science research model or scientific-agent system (for example a successor in the GPT-Rosalind line, a DeepMind/Isomorphic research agent, or an open evaluation submission) will report on LifeSciBench, or on a comparably artifact-grounded successor benchmark, an artifact-task pass rate within 10 percentage points of its text-only pass rate — down from today's roughly 17-point spread — while keeping overall accuracy at or above GPT-Rosalind's current level. The mechanism is tool-and-parser grounding rather than larger context windows: native readers for sequence/structure/assay formats, file-aware tool use, and rubric-targeted post-training on artifact-bearing tasks are all tractable and directly aimed at the measured failure. Closing the gap would not deliver autonomous wet-lab science, but it would convert the single most-cited objection to research agents into a quantified, shrinking number, which is the necessary precondition before any lab trusts these systems with real experimental data.

reasoning.because: GPT-Rosalind fell 45.1%→28.1% on LifeSciBench once a task needed a real data file or URL
reasoning.given: the artifact gap is the cleanest cited weakness, targetable with file-aware tools and parsers
reasoning.so_that: the next research-agent will optimize artifact grounding directly, shrinking the text-vs-artifact accuracy spread
reasoning.landing: By H2 2027 a named life-science agent posts a sub-10pt LifeSciBench artifact gap
reasoning.plain_language: Soon a science AI will get almost as good at reading real lab data files as it is at discussing biology in words.

summary: LifeSciBench's durable signal is the artifact gap: GPT-Rosalind scored 45.1% on text-only tasks but 28.1% once a task needed a real data file or URL. The prediction: by H2 2027 a named life-science agent cuts that ~17-point spread below 10 on LifeSciBench or a comparable benchmark.
